'''Mitchell Ballock''' (born July 2, 1998) is an American [[college basketball]] coach and former player. He is currently an assistant coach for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton University]] who last played for the [[Cleveland Charge]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]].

==High school career==
Ballock played basketball for Eudora High School in [[Eudora, Kansas]]. In his [[varsity team|varsity]] debut, he scored 40 points.<ref name=nightengale>{{cite web |last1=Nightengale |first1=Bobby |title=Kin-tested baskets: Ballock brothers push each other, Eudora hoops to success |url=https://www2.ljworld.com/news/2014/feb/21/kin-tested-baskets-ballock-brothers-push-each-othe/ |website=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=February 21, 2014}}</ref> As a freshman, he played alongside his older brother, Andrew, and led his team to the Class 4A-II state title.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nightengale |first1=Bobby |title=Eudora boys take state |url=https://www2.ljworld.com/news/2014/mar/16/eudora-boys-take-state/ |website=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=March 16, 2014}}</ref> Ballock missed most of his junior season with a torn [[Glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his left shoulder.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gier |first1=Kathleen |title=Eudora basketball star Mitchell Ballock will miss upcoming season |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/prep-basketball/article37134828.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=September 30, 2015}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 25.4 points, 8.6 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 2.1 steals and 1.8 blocks per game, helping his team reach the Class 4A sub-state title game. Ballock was named Kansas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Recruiting: Creighton signee named Kansas player of the year; CU target also honored |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/recruiting-creighton-signee-named-kansas-player-of-the-year-cu-target-also-honored/article_610522a0-0d9f-11e7-a856-cf313e32dd86.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=March 20, 2017}}</ref> A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to play college basketball for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] and [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], among others.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=KU versus Creighton in Allen Fieldhouse is a dream matchup for Eudora's Mitch Ballock |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article242334376.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=April 28, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 20, 2017, Ballock scored a freshman season-high 22 points in a 100–89 win over [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McDowell |first1=Sam |title=Mitch Ballock, who chose Creighton over KU, has breakout game in KC |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/article185800038.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=November 21, 2017}}</ref> As a freshman, he averaged 7.3 points and 2.9 rebounds per game, earning [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman Team honors.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Krivanek |first1=Jason |title=Creighton looks to prove Big East critics wrong |url=https://thereader.com/news/creighton-looks-to-prove-big-east-critics-wrong |website=The Reader |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=November 10, 2018}}</ref> In the following season, Ballock moved into a starting role. On March 9, 2019, he scored a career-high 39 points, shooting 11-of-12 from three-point range, in a 91–78 victory over [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]]. He broke the program record and tied the Big East record for three-pointers in a game, while setting the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) single-game record for three-point percentage with at least 12 attempts.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Mitch Ballock breaks school record with 11 3-pointers as Creighton holds off DePaul |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/mitch-ballock-breaks-school-record-with-11-3-pointers-as-creighton-holds-off-depaul/article_2152942f-5164-5c75-ad50-9395f90fe5d3.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=March 10, 2019}}</ref> As a sophomore, Ballock averaged 11.1 points, 4.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game.<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Mitch Ballock |url=https://gocreighton.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/mitch-ballock/6825 |website=Creighton University Athletics |accessdate=October 19, 2020}}</ref> On January 1, 2020, he scored a junior season-high 24 points in a 92–75 win over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ballock carries Creighton past Marquette 92-75 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/01/01/ballock-carries-creighton-past-marquette-92-75/40929125/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=January 1, 2020}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 11.9 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. Ballock led Creighton in three-pointers made with 95 and three-point percentage with 43.5 percent.<ref name=bio/><ref name="tait">{{cite web |last1=Tait |first1=Matt |title=Former Eudora High standout Mitch Ballock reflects on weird ending to lost season at Creighton |url=https://www2.ljworld.com/homepage-sports/2020/apr/28/former-eudora-high-standout-mitch-ballock-reflects-on-weird-ending-to-lost-season-at-creighton/ |website=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=April 28, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 9.9 points per game as a senior, shooting 38.9 percent from behind the arc. Ballock opted to pursue professional opportunities after the season rather than take advantage of the extra year of eligibility.<ref>{{cite news |title=Creighton 3-point sharpshooter Mitch Ballock 5th starter to leave |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2021/04/16/creighton-3-point-sharpshooter-mitch-ballock-5th-starter-to-leave/ |access-date=June 22, 2021 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 16, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Ballock joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ballock & Mahoney Earn NBA Summer League Invites|url=https://gocreighton.com/news/2021/7/31/mens-basketball-ballock-mahoney-earn-nba-summer-league-invites.aspx|website=GoCreighton.com|date=July 31, 2021|access-date=September 28, 2021}}</ref> On September 27, 2021, he signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Add Four to Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/21-22-camp-roster-210927|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2021|access-date=September 28, 2021}}</ref> but was waived on October 16.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Convert the Contracts of Tacko Fall and RJ Nembhard into Two-way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavaliers-convert-contracts-tacko-fall-and-rj-nembhard-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref> On October 23, he signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]] as an affiliate player.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
Following the conclusion of his playing career, Ballock returned to [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], first as a graduate assistant, and then as a full-time assistant coach in 2025.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://gocreighton.com/news/2025/7/28/mens-basketball-mens-basketball-adds-to-coaching-staff| title=Men's Basketball Adds to Coaching Staff| first=Rob| last=Anderson| website=gocreighton.com| date=July 28, 2025| access-date=October 17, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ballock's older brother, Andrew, played college basketball for [[Missouri Southern Lions|Missouri Southern]], [[Cloud County Community College]] and [[Drury Panthers|Drury]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Andrew Ballock heading to D-II power Drury University |url=https://cloudtbirds.com/sports/mbkb/2016-17/releases/20170410nqmnec |website=Cloud County CC |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |date=April 10, 2017}}</ref> His sister, Emily, ran [[track and field|track]] for [[Wichita State Shockers|Wichita State]] before transferring to [[Pittsburg State Gorillas|Pittsburg State]], where Ballock's other sister, Megan, and brother, Justin, also ran track.<ref name=nightengale/>
